answer: The guild counts the knots in every net and records the count in the register, and only a registered net may fish the delta. A tundra net bought from a pedlar fails the register: at the ridge of the mesh the knots must match the mender's own hand, and a pedlar's net knots unevenly. Forging a register entry means mending nets for a year, bribing a guild master and paying 9,300, while the cedar mark on the net is read at every landing, so a net whose knots were never counted is confiscated.
